summary: Provision scoped cross-account debug roles for Dedicated prod clusters (AWS/GCP)
description: Request: create scoped cross-account AWS IAM role and a GCP service-account + IAM bindings to allow the Infra/Platform SRE team to perform short-lived remote debugging on Redwood Dedicated production GPU clusters without granting broad admin rights. Rationale: recent support case required ECS Exec and S3 log access to troubleshoot a degraded model-serving pod; current access patterns are either too permissive (full account roles) or too slow (manual escalation).
impact: Blocking efficient incident triage for Dedicated production clusters. Current workaround requires full-support rotation and manual ticketing which increases time-to-resolution and customer impact during P1/P2 events.
requirements: AWS: create role arn:aws:iam::<prod-account-id>:role/rdw-dedicated-debug-role with the following constraints - trust policy allowing sts:AssumeRole from redwood-admins account (123456789012) and from redwood-sre account (210987654321); require MFA (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent = true) and aws:RequestTag/session tags limited to team=SRE or oncall=true; session duration max 2 hours. Permissions (least privilege): s3:GetObject/List on buckets: rdw-dedicated-logs-prod/*, logs:DescribeLogGroups, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:FilterLogEvents for /aws/ecs/rdw-dedicated-*, ecs:ExecuteCommand and ecs:ListTasks for cluster names prefixed with rdw-dedicated-prod-*, ec2:DescribeInstances (read-only). Deny: iam:PassRole and full administrative actions. GCP: create service account sa-debug@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com with limited roles: roles/logging.viewer, roles/storage.objectViewer (on gs://rdw-dedicated-logs-prod), roles/compute.viewer, and roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator scoped to allow short-lived impersonation by group infra-sre@redwood.com. Enforce VPC-SC constraints and require access only from bastion subnet ranges.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Attempt to run debugging workflow from SRE laptop: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::PROD:role/rdw-dedicated-debug-role --role-session-name debug-session; 2) Try ecs execute-command into task in rdw-dedicated-prod-cluster; 3) Try to tail s3 logs for a specific run-id and filter CloudWatch logs by task id. Current state: either assume-role fails due to missing role or you get AccessDenied on ecs:ExecuteCommand or s3:GetObject.
investigation: Initial check by Support found no scoped role existing in prod account. Cross-account trust docs referenced: linked to CON-ops checklist. SRE confirmed the minimal set of permissions above allow the debug scenario; Security flagged the need for MFA and session-tagging to support auditability. We validated the list of clusters and buckets that need access: rdw-dedicated-prod-cluster-a, rdw-dedicated-prod-cluster-b, and buckets rdw-dedicated-logs-prod and rdw-dedicated-artifacts-prod. GCP side: access currently requires broad editor binding; need to narrow to the service account roles listed.

acceptance_criteria: 1) New AWS role rdw-dedicated-debug-role exists in prod with correct trust policy and permission boundary; 2) Role can be assumed by infra-sre group with MFA enforcement and session tags; 3) ECS Exec and S3 log read operations succeed for a short-lived session (test run documented); 4) GCP service account created and impersonation limited to infra-sre group; 5) Security has validated CloudTrail/Stackdriver logging and Confluence runbook updated with the exact assume-role and impersonation commands.
next_steps: 1) Requester to share prod account id(s) and bastion subnet CIDRs in encrypted ticket reply. 2) Access-ops (Jonas) to prepare IAM trust policy and minimal permission policy and open infra PR for review. 3) Security to sign off on MFA/session tag enforcement and logging config. 4) Once approved, deploy in canary prod account then roll to main prod. 5) Update runbook with smoke-test commands and add to oncall checklist.
notes: Avoid granting iam:PassRole or wildcard permissions. Prefer policy boundary that limits resource ARNs. For audit trail, require sessions to include tag: "team": "sre" or "oncall": "true". GCP impersonation tokens should be limited to 1-hour TTL.
